chapter: Brown's Band and Tom in Chicago
title: Tom's band in Chicago and New York, via Ray Lopez's letters
summary: Brown relays Lopez's reports: Lamb's Cafe packed in Chicago, a cool reception in New York, members scattering.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: If you can play some of those old records, Amanda, I wonder first, though, if you have anything more to add about Tom going to Chicago, since he's not here to speak for himself, anything else that you think he wanted to know about himself and the things that he originated and first started?

Well, I was away from Tom and all the boys at that particular time and in a different line of business entirely with Chief Metalworks, so therefore, I can order to tell you what he'd write and how the band was going along and what letters that I received from Ray Lopez, who would write me now and then. Gus Mule would never write me, and Tom would very seldom write me at that time. But Ray Lopez told me, he says, you know, he said, when we first got to Chicago, he says, the people thought we were drunk. They thought we were crazy. They refused to come into the cafe. He says, they just peeped in there and looked in there and they saw some fuller sitting on the piano playing and the other baller doing something else. He says, my God, he said, Lamb come to Tom, they say, say, he says, something's wrong. He says, those people are not coming in. Well, he says, the next day, he says, I happened to be down in the loop and I met some actors that were in the theater there and they said, Ray, what are you doing in Chicago? Boy, he says, I'm here with Brown's band. You are? He said, put that band down there? He says, sure. He says, my goodness, where are you playing at? He said, Lamb's Cafe. So they call up and reserve seats in Lamb's Cafe. And from then on, the damn place start being packed. And Ray Lopez tells me that the people were waiting a block and two blocks long, waiting to gain admittance at the Lamb's Cafe at that particular time. So it really went over fast in Chicago. The people accepted it and took over to it very quickly. But when they went to New York, Ray says, the people didn't take to it so quick. They went into it as an act, as a rule bag. And every place they played, you know, the people couldn't get to drift the things, you know? And because they didn't go over so well, they didn't get to bookies. So finally, some of the boys left New York and left Tom and Ray up there. So they had to find it out the best way they could. So Tom drifted in with other bands and Ray Lopez drifted in with other bands too. Ray Mueller, who played at the College Inn, and later on joined Whiteman.
We're trying to get to talk to Ray. And he's out in Hawthorne? Hawthorne, California.
I'll give you the address before you go.
Good, fine, then. And one more thing.
